subject.title: Gateway crash-loops on startup when legacy `plugins/installs.json` conflicts with shared SQLite plugin index (`doctor --fix` does not reconcile)

question: When legacy plugin metadata conflicts with the shared SQLite index, should doctor automatically preserve verified SQLite state and archive the legacy file, or require an explicit operator choice for every conflict?
rationale: The recovery defect is clear, but choosing install-intent precedence can discard a deliberately selected source or path and therefore requires an explicit product rule.

options.title: Auto-reconcile verified SQLite
options.body: When SQLite points to a present, integrity-matching installed artifact, preserve it, archive the legacy file, and require explicit repair only when verification fails.

options.title: Always require operator choice
options.body: Show both records in doctor and require the operator to select the canonical install intent before archiving either source.

options.title: Relax readiness only
options.body: Leave conflicting records untouched and downgrade this migration result to non-fatal, accepting persistent warnings and unresolved duplicate state.

recommendation.title: Auto-reconcile verified SQLite
recommendation.body: When SQLite points to a present, integrity-matching installed artifact, preserve it, archive the legacy file, and require explicit repair only when verification fails.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent install-index consolidation and persistence work is the closest direct history signal for defining the reconciliation contract.
